sources.entry: See the Product management section on my entrepreneurship-resources list of resources.

summary.one_liner: A curated, link-heavy list of entrepreneurship resources (articles, books, talks, slides) organized by topic, with a Product management section that is one of its many categories.
summary.what_it_does: The README is an annotated index of links and short takeaways about starting and running companies. It opens with generic resources (books and playbooks, articles) and then groups material into dozens of topic headings such as Acquisition, Pricing, Pitch decks, Sales, Metrics, MVP, Hiring, and Product management. Entries are mostly titles or links with occasional bullet-point summaries of the key ideas. Items are tagged with emoji for list, book, video, slides, and must-read. The Product management section lists articles on product teams, product managers, product sense, and related topics, alongside pointers to other lists by the same author. The README itself is the content; it does not describe installable software.
use_cases: Finding reading material on startup strategy and founding
Looking up articles on product management and product-market fit
Browsing pricing, SaaS, and B2B sales advice
Preparing a pitch deck by studying examples
Learning about MVPs and lean experimentation
how_to_run: Open the README in a browser or on GitHub and navigate by the Table of Contents
notable: Organized into many topic sections covering the whole startup lifecycle
Short annotated takeaways from well-known sources such as Paul Graham, Jason Cohen, and Y Combinator
Cross-links to related lists by the same author for engineering management and professional programming
Emoji legend marks books, videos, slides, and must-read items
caveats: Link-only list: content lives on external sites and may go stale or disappear
Coverage is uneven, with some sections holding only one or two entries
